questions: Does wheel_radius 0.025 m lower max_error below 0.06 m on the s-bend and slalom, or does progress fall because the robot is now too slow to cover the course?
Does steering_oscillation and control_effort fall relative to iteration 4 (0.03 m radius), which would confirm that overshoot at speed is the limit?
Is completion_time measurable on any track at this speed, and what progress is reached before the first off-track event?
Do line-loss events stay at or below iteration 4 levels (oval 0, s-bend about 0.95, slalom about 0.85)?

intent: Test the opposite direction to iteration 5. Revert to the iteration 4 design (best so far, 58.5) and change only wheel_radius, from 0.03 to 0.025 m, to see whether lower speed and turn rate reduce the overshoot that causes off-track ends on the s-bend and slalom.
learning: Iterations 5 and 6 showed that both a larger wheel_radius and a heavier mass reduce usable progress on the s-bend, so the limit appears to be overshoot and lag at high speed and inertia, not too little speed. Iteration 2 (shorter, lighter body with y=0.07) also hurt, so the best layout remains y=0.05 with the 7-sensor, 16 mm array. This iteration tests the speed direction downward at wheel_radius 0.025 m. If progress falls with no gain in max_error, the optimum is near 0.03 m and the next test should be mass 0.6 kg at 0.03 m radius, to check whether lower inertia helps once speed is held constant.
rationale: Race evidence from the last three iterations is consistent. Iteration 4 (wheel_track 0.08 m, wheel_radius 0.03 m, mass 0.8 kg, 7 sensors at y=0.05 m, 16 mm footprints, body 0.18 x 0.12 m) is still the best design at 58.5. Iteration 5 raised wheel_radius to 0.04 m and fell to 41.4, with s-bend progress collapsing from 0.185 to 0.0625. Iteration 6 raised mass to 1.0 kg and fell to 42.7, with s-bend progress dropping to 0.065. Both changes hurt the s-bend most, and control effort stayed high. Every run still ends off_track with max_error pinned at the 0.06 m floor, and line loss is now rare, so sensor coverage is not the limit. The off-track floor cannot be moved by body width, since max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4) stays at 0.06 m. Both extra speed (radius) and extra inertia (mass) reduced usable progress, which suggests the robot is overshooting or lagging on bends rather than being too slow. The one lever that has not been tested in this direction is lower ground speed. I therefore revert to iteration 4 and reduce wheel_radius from 0.03 to 0.025 m (the lower end of the range I have tested is 0.03, and 0.025 is an unexplored step), keeping mass at 0.8 kg. This lowers ground speed and turn rate together, so it tests whether the overshoot that drives the off-track ends eases at lower speed. Expected result: s-bend and slalom progress rise above 0.185 and max_error drops below 0.063 m, at the cost of some completion_time. Risk: slower ground speed may leave progress too low to finish within 3 s, in which case the speed/turn trade-off has a sweet spot near 0.03 m.
